primary.statement: Trend strength improves breakout-family outcomes (higher E[R] and/or better rank spread when a Breakout SIGNAL_META key fires).
primary.result_note: Pooled breakout Spearman(n_passed, R)=0.166, n=18281. Family-heterogeneous: VOL_SQUEEZE carries the lift; BREAKOUT_52W does not.

primary.statement: rs_cs_v1 improves breakout and momentum family outcomes.
primary.result_note: Pooled breakout+momentum Spearman(RS, R)=0.306, n=32816. VOL_SQUEEZE and MOMENTUM drive it; BREAKOUT_52W is UNSTABLE.

primary.statement: Trend and/or RS reduce adverse-selection tails (bottom-decile R, stop-before-1R, large MAE). Report as RISK_FILTER_VALUE, not automatically ALPHA.
primary.result_note: Bottom-decile rate lower for structure_pass than non-trend (delta -0.068). Label RISK_FILTER_VALUE where mean E[R] does not lift.

primary.statement: Trend and RS add information beyond existing momentum scoring (mom_score, momentum_5d) and the production technical score.
primary.result_note: Residual Spearman after mom_score is 0.052 (Trend) and 0.071 (RS). Detectable at n=120270; economically small. After production score, RS residual rho=0.215.

primary.statement: The value of Trend/RS differs materially by strategy family (not one universal policy).
primary.result_note: Std of family Trend deltas=0.101 (15 families with n>=30). No p-value; FDR does not reject. Policy table is the evidence.

exploratory: Joint A/B/C/D attribution inside each family (strategy alone / +strong trend / +strong RS / +both).
RS bucket monotonicity including 95-99 vs 70-79 (descriptive; do not move the 70 cutoff).
